# elizaOS Discord - 2026-07-31

## Summary

### Solana Trading Plugin Release

pnllabs_13084 announced the release of a new Solana trading plugin (@pnllabs/plugin-pnllabs) designed to provide pre-transaction verification for Solana agents. The plugin offers several key features including wallet trust scoring based on realized on-chain profit and loss, token safety checks, real trade cost analysis, and funding forensics. The team conducted an audit of 30 tracked 'smart money' wallets and discovered that approximately half were actually losing money rather than profiting. The plugin is available through npm and offers a free tier that does not require an API key. For usage beyond the free tier, the plugin uses a pay-per-call pricing model via x402. The developer is actively seeking community feedback on the implementation.

# elizaOS Discord - 2026-07-29

## Summary

### Project Development Status

ElizaOS v3 has been released and is available through the main GitHub repository. Shaw continues active development on GitHub, with the Eliza framework being utilized by many builders for additional projects. Development work on both Milady and the Eliza v3 app is ongoing, though no firm release dates have been announced. The project is currently seeking funding and investors for expansion purposes.

### Community Communication Concerns

Community members expressed frustration about the lack of updates on official communication channels. Multiple platforms including X/Twitter, Discord, and Farcaster were reported as inactive since late May 2026. This created a perceived communication gap between active development work happening on GitHub and community engagement on social channels. Shaw did post about the Eliza app on X/Twitter recently, though regular updates remain limited.

### Legal Resolution

A legal settlement was reached with the lawsuit dismissed with prejudice on July 8, 2026. The court retained 30-day jurisdiction to enforce the settlement terms.

### Tokenomics Proposal

A community member proposed a new tokenomics model requiring users to purchase and lock tokens to access plugins and services. The suggested model aims to prevent sell-offs and increase token value through utility-based demand.

### Team Structure

Discussion included requests to bring odlitime back to the team to support ongoing development efforts.

## FAQ

**Q: Has ElizaOS v3 been released?**
A: Yes, Eliza v3 has been released and is available by cloning the main repository on GitHub. It is receiving regular updates.

**Q: Why are the official communication channels inactive?**
A: While development continues actively on GitHub, official channels like X/Twitter, Discord, and Farcaster have been largely inactive since late May 2026. The team is focused on development work rather than community updates.

**Q: What is the status of the lawsuit?**
A: The lawsuit was dismissed with prejudice on July 8, 2026, following a legal settlement. The court retained 30-day jurisdiction to enforce the settlement.

**Q: When will Milady and Eliza v3 app be released?**
A: Development continues on both projects, but no firm release dates have been announced.

**Q: Is the ElizaOS framework being used by other developers?**
A: Yes, many builders are using the Eliza framework for their own projects.

**Q: Is the project seeking funding?**
A: Yes, Shaw mentioned seeking funding and investors for expansion.

## Help Interactions

**Helper:** j_choy
**Helpee:** paolin_62616
**Resolution:** Clarified that Shaw is actively developing on GitHub and that development work is ongoing despite lack of communication on official channels.

**Helper:** om1d_sa
**Helpee:** Community
**Resolution:** Confirmed that v3 has been released and is receiving updates, directing users to clone the main repository for access.

## Action Items

### Technical

- Seek funding and investors for project expansion (mentioned by Shaw)
- Continue development on Milady and Eliza v3 app (ongoing work by Shaw)

### Features

- Consider implementing tokenomics model requiring users to buy and lock tokens to access plugins/services (proposed by paolin_62616)

### Documentation

- Improve communication on official channels including X/Twitter, Discord, and Farcaster (implied by paolin_62616's concerns)
- Consider bringing odlitime back to the team (requested by om1d_sa)

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Jul 26 - 1, 2026)

## Executive Summary
This week, the ElizaOS team focused on hardening our core infrastructure to ensure a stable, reliable foundation for our growing agent ecosystem. By resolving critical production issues and streamlining our development processes, we have improved the framework's resilience while making significant progress on the new "Agentic Parent Suite" for household coordination.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Strengthening Platform Reliability**
_Goal: We aimed to eliminate production errors and ensure that our agents operate consistently and predictably._
- Resolved critical failures in agent management, ensuring that agents can be created and removed without system errors ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17260)).
- Improved the accuracy of agent monitoring and data tracking, ensuring that user interactions and wallet balances are recorded correctly ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17140)).
- Optimized our internal testing and deployment pipelines to prevent system crashes and speed up development workflows ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17238)).

**Expanding Agent Capabilities**
_Goal: We are building new features that allow agents to handle complex, real-world tasks like household management and on-chain execution._
- Advanced the "Agentic Parent Suite," a new initiative designed to help agents manage household schedules and coordination ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/issues/17175)).
- Began integrating the Aomi plugin, which will enable agents to perform more sophisticated on-chain executions ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/issues/17288)).

## Repository Spotlights

### elizaos/eliza
- Fixed critical bugs in agent lifecycle management, specifically resolving issues where agent deletion would fail due to data mismatches ([elizaos/eliza#17260](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17260), [elizaos/eliza#17251](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17251)).
- Introduced new diagnostic tools to allow for safer inspection of agent states in staging environments ([elizaos/eliza#17189](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17189), [elizaos/eliza#17196](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17196)).
- Refined agent startup and monitoring logic to prevent legitimate tasks from being incorrectly flagged as errors ([elizaos/eliza#17292](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17292)).
- Updated core development dependencies to maintain environment parity and improve overall project health ([elizaos/eliza#17291](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17291)).
- Successfully resolved project coordination issues, fostering better collaboration on agent-related tasks ([elizaos/eliza#17204](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/issues/17204)).

# Overall Project Monthly Summary (July 2026)

## Executive Summary
In July 2026, the ElizaOS project focused on transforming the framework into a production-ready ecosystem by hardening security, improving financial reliability, and expanding agent capabilities. These efforts ensure that our AI agents are not only more intelligent and versatile but also operate within a secure, stable, and commercially viable infrastructure.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Building a Secure and Reliable Foundation**
_Goal: We aimed to make the platform safer for commercial use and more dependable for developers by removing technical debt and strengthening security._
- We implemented robust financial safeguards and secure payment systems to support monetization ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/10942), [#11606](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/11606)).
- We hardened our security by protecting sensitive model credentials and creating safer, isolated environments for agent operations ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/11660), [#11402](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/11402)).
- We established strict error-handling policies to replace silent failures with clear, actionable reporting, significantly improving system reliability ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/13236)).

**Advancing Agent Intelligence and Versatility**
_Goal: We wanted to make our agents smarter and more capable of handling complex, real-world scenarios._
- We expanded the LifeOps framework with over 240 new persona scenarios, allowing agents to act more naturally in diverse situations ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/12356)).
- We upgraded our core intelligence by adopting the latest Gemma-4 benchmarks and creating a new pipeline to train smaller, more efficient models ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/11196), [#11891](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/11891)).

**Improving User Accessibility and Experience**
_Goal: We focused on making the ElizaOS experience seamless across mobile and desktop devices._
- We introduced voice-first features for mobile users, including keyboard extensions and live activity tracking for voice sessions ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/12685), [#12503](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/12503)).
- We modernized the desktop experience with faster communication tools and a more visually appealing command-line interface ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/12485), [#11591](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/11591)).

## Repository Spotlights

### elizaos/eliza
- Launched monetization tools, including an influencer marketplace and secure payment rails via Stripe and OxaPay ([elizaos/eliza#10942](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/10942), [#11606](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/11606), [#10863](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/10863)).
- Enhanced security by implementing vendor-neutral model gateways and encrypted sandbox environments ([elizaos/eliza#11660](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/11660), [#11402](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/11402)).
- Integrated 240+ persona scenarios into the LifeOpsBench to improve agent behavior ([elizaos/eliza#12356](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/12356)).
- Completed the Gemma-4-31b benchmark cutover and deployed a fine-tuning pipeline for `eliza-1-2b` ([elizaos/eliza#11196](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/11196), [#11891](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/11891)).
- Added mobile-native voice features and improved desktop TUI aesthetics ([elizaos/eliza#12685](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/12685), [#12503](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/12503), [#12485](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/12485), [#11591](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/11591)).
- Standardized repository scripts and implemented a "fail-closed" error policy to improve maintainability ([elizaos/eliza#13236](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/13236), [#13064](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/13064)).
